title: Fibre-generic detection of vertical principal ideals
statement: Let $V$ be a valuation domain, meaning a subring of its fraction field $K$ such that $a$ or $a^{-1}$ belongs to $V$ for every $a\in K^\times$ [def-weil-field]. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Let $B$ be a flat finitely presented commutative $V$-algebra [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose that all its fibres are geometrically reduced: for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset V$ and field extension $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, the ring $B\otimes_V L$ has no nonzero nilpotents [def-weil-residue-field]. Put $B_K=B\otimes_VK$. Let $f,g\in B$ have invertible images in $B_K$. For every $\mathfrak p\subset V$ and every generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component of $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_V\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-irreducible-components], let $\mathfrak q_\xi\subset B$ be its inverse-image prime. If $fB_{\mathfrak q_\xi}=gB_{\mathfrak q_\xi}$ for every such $\xi$, then $fB=gB$. Here $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is localization at a prime [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; no Noetherian hypothesis on $V$ is imposed.

source.place: Agent-reconstructed finite-height valuation version of detection at fibre-generic points. Background only: Tag 05CB, lemma-zero-at-weakly-ass-zero; that lemma detects a module at all weakly associated primes and does not itself identify the required primes over a valuation quotient. This additional identification is part of this unsplit assertion.

proof.text: Put $U=V\setminus\{0\}$. For every $s\in U$, multiplication by $s$ on the domain $V$ is injective; [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] applied with the flat $V$-module $B$ makes multiplication by $s$ on $B$ injective. The identifications $V\otimes_VB=B$ send $a\otimes b$ to $ab$, with inverse $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. Identify $B_K=B\otimes_VK$ with $U^{-1}B$: the mutually inverse maps are $b\otimes(a/s)\mapsto ab/s$ and $b/s\mapsto b\otimes(1/s)$. They respect the fraction relation and bilinearity, and their composites fix the displayed generators [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The localization criterion $b/1=0\iff sb=0$ for some $s\in U$ now shows that $B\to B_K$ is injective.

source.place: Elementary application of flat tensor injectivity and the fraction relation; the displayed maps give the tensor/localization identification explicitly.

proof.text: Fix $h\in\{f,g\}$. Since $h$ is a unit in $B_K=U^{-1}B$, write its inverse as $b/s$ with $b\in B$, $s\in U$. The equality $hb/s=1$ means $t(hb-s)=0$ for some $t\in U$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; Step 1 cancels $t$, giving $hb=s$ in $B$. Multiplication by $b$ is injective: $bx=0$ implies $sx=hbx=0$, hence $x=0$ by Step 1. Consequently the $B$-linear map $i_h:B/hB\to B/sB$, $x+hB\mapsto bx+sB$, is well-defined and injective: if $bx=sy=hby$, cancel $b$ to obtain $x=hy$. There is a $B$-linear isomorphism $(V/sV)\otimes_VB\cong B/sB$: send $(a+sV)\otimes x$ to $ax+sB$, and send $x+sB$ back to $(1+sV)\otimes x$. These maps are well-defined by the quotient and tensor relations, and their composites fix every class and pure tensor [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Explicit denominator equation, cancellation, quotient injection and mutually inverse tensor-quotient maps; no valuation-chain induction.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q$ be minimal over $\operatorname{Ann}_B(x)$ for an element $x\in B/hB$; this is what weakly associated means here. Since $i_h$ is $B$-linear and injective, $\operatorname{Ann}_B(i_h(x))=\operatorname{Ann}_B(x)$: either annihilation equation implies the other by linearity and injectivity. Thus $\mathfrak q$ is weakly associated to $B/sB\cong(V/sV)\otimes_VB$. Apply [lem-trf-flat-tensor-weakass-fibre] with $R=V$, $S=B$, and $M=V/sV$. Its hypotheses are exactly the assumed finite presentation and flatness of $B$; it requires neither a Noetherian base nor finite generation of ideals of $V$. For $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap V$, $C=B\otimes_V\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and the corresponding fibre prime $\overline{\mathfrak q}$, it gives $\overline{\mathfrak q}=\operatorname{Ann}_C(z)$ for some $z\in C$.

source.place: Tag 05IG, lemma-weak-bourbaki-pre, N=B and M=V/sV, forward implication; exact preservation of annihilators by the injection of Step 2.

proof.text:
Take $(r,h)$ to be either $(f,g)$ or $(g,f)$, and suppose that $x=r+hB$ is nonzero in $B/hB$. Its annihilator $I$ is proper, since $1x=x
e0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal] choose a prime $\mathfrak q$ minimal over $I$. It is weakly associated to $B/hB$ by the witness $x$, so Steps 3--4 identify it with a fibre-generic prime. source.place: Minimal prime over the annihilator and the explicit fraction equation; this proves detection directly rather than invoking an extra localization-detection lemma.

proof.text: For $(r,h)=(f,g)$, Step 5 gives $f\in gB$, hence $fB\subseteq gB$ by multiplication. For $(r,h)=(g,f)$ it gives the reverse inclusion. Antisymmetry yields $fB=gB$.

source.place: Elementary multiplication of generators and antisymmetry of ideal inclusion.
